source_text: Iterum dicis: "Quod carnem suam nullus oderit". Quis enim hoc negat? Sed tamen disciplinae rigore asseris conterendam. … Dimissis itaque in Baptismo peccatis omnibus, id est omnibus concupiscentiae fetibus, si illic etiam ipsa consumpta est, quomodo contra eam ne concipiat, dimicant sancti "livore corporis, paedore membrorum, contritione carnis"? quae verba tua sunt.
pass_a_gloss: Again you say: 'That no one hates his own flesh'. For who denies this? But nevertheless by the rigour of discipline you assert (it) to be crushed. All sins therefore having been remitted in Baptism, that is all the offspring of concupiscence, if there also it itself was consumed, how against it, lest it conceive, do the saints fight 'with the bruise of the body, the filth of the members, the crushing of the flesh'? which are your words.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “Again you say ‘that no one hates his own flesh’ (Ephesians 5:29). Who denies it? Yet you assert that it must be broken down by the rigor of discipline.”

“So, when all sins are forgiven in baptism, that is, all the offspring of desire, if desire itself was also used up there, how do the saints fight against it, so that it may not conceive, ‘with bruising of the body, squalor of the limbs, breaking down of the flesh’? These are your words.”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Inline in Pass B; verse text checked against the quoted words.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
